messages:
Maya: We did a short spike on soft-lease credits this morning to reduce head-of-line blocking for tiny requests. tl;dr: seems promising but a couple of weird long-tail cases popped up.
Ben: Nice, what did you measure?
Maya: P95 dropped ~15% for 1-8 token requests under 75% load. P99 unchanged in one cluster where we saw eviction jitter.
Sasha: eviction jitter = bursts where many tiny batches are kicked mid-flight?
Maya: exactly. When a mid-sized tenant suddenly reclaims headroom, the soft-lease cleanup causes multiple microbatches to be preempted and requeued leading to a 250ms hiccup.
Ryan: do we have a repro? logs or a trace?
Maya: captured traces. key snippets: ```
# simplified timeline
enqueue tiny req A
coalesce -> schedule to slot S
slot stolen by tenant X reclaim -> A evicted -> A re-enqueue -> waits for next coalesce window
```
Maya: That extra re-enqueue is the source of the tail.
Ben: Could we do a cheap fastpath: if evicted and remaining seq len <= 8 tokens, reattach to in-flight slot if slot still running and has capacity? basically piggyback instead of full re-enqueue.
Sasha: piggyback requires slot visibility across admission boundary. We currently have a hard boundary to avoid coupling scheduler internals to slot state.
Maya: Right, but maybe a small shim: public method on slot manager like `TryAttach(shortCtx) -> bool` with strict invariants.
Ryan: that API smells OK, but we need to reason about correctness under preemption. If slot gets released mid-attach we need a safe rollback.
Ben: implement with compare-and-swap lease id: attach succeeds only if lease id unchanged. cheap and lock-free.
Sasha: plus metric: attach_failures for telemetry so we can see if piggyback helps.
Maya: alternative was to increase coalesce frequency for tiny requests which helps tail but worsens throughput and increases GPU kernel overhead. tradeoff.
Ben: I like piggyback + metric. Low-risk, targeted. fallback: degrade to re-enqueue.
Maya: Implementation plan: 1) add `TryAttach(shortCtx, leaseId)` on SlotManager 2) atomically verify lease 3) if success, update KV cache pointer and add small accounting token 4) observability: attach_latency, attach_success, attach_fail
Ryan: don't forget to gate on tenant QoS class. we shouldn't allow piggyback to bypass tenant isolation rules.
Sasha: good call. Gate: only allow piggyback for QoS <= burstable and body_size <= 8 tokens.
Maya: rough patch diff I pasted in #eng-runtime-sandbox. deploy-bot: can you run a canary across staging-2?
deploy-bot: triggered canary: slot-piggyback-2026-03-20 -> staging-2 (status: queued)
infra-bot: reminder: if this touches SlotManager state machine, we need a migration for older dedicated nodes; add feature flag.
Maya: yes feature flag `slot_piggyback_opt` default off. will flip in canary.
Ben: also add a safety throttle: max_attaches_per_window per slot to avoid thundering attach storms.
Sasha: question: does piggyback complicate KV cache consistency? if we attach mid-slot, we must ensure the KV cache for the slot includes the prompt prefix used by the tiny request.
Maya: piggyback only allowed when request prefix is subset of the slot's cached prefix (cheap prefix-check). if not subset, fall back to re-enqueue.
Ryan: sounds solid. For rollout: canary -> 24h perf tests with synthetic mix (tiny-heavy spike, medium steady) -> roll 10% -> 50% -> global. Collect P50/95/99 and attach metrics.
Sasha: also add a debug trace tag: `attach_candidate=true` so we can surface failures quickly in tracing UI.
Maya: I'll post the RFC follow-up doc in RFCs/ after we validate. For now this thread is the design check.
Ben: one more edge: what about streaming responses? attaching mid-slot into a streaming generator might complicate token offsets.
Maya: piggyback only for non-streaming or streaming-without-early-flush; otherwise force re-enqueue. We'll enumerate in the doc.
Ryan: ok. If you want, I can help write the safe-attach unit tests around lease races.
Maya: please do. I'll open PR with feature flag, metrics, and tests.
Ben: :thumbsup: excited to see less noisy tails.
Sasha: thanks Maya — great pragmatic improvement.
Maya: thanks all, will update thread with PR link and canary results later.
